alt.text: Type option and the token sheet

flow.text: The flow — start, log, compare, rest

typenote.text: Type stand-in: Comic Neue renders here because Google Fonts does not serve Comic Relief. Shapes are close enough to judge; a real build keeps your bundled ComicRelief ttf.

wiring.text:
Board 2 → 3: tapping the "Last time 65 × 8" pill opens the history sheet. Previous sessions stay one tap away, never on screen by default.

Board 2 → 4: logging the set swaps the input card for the rest timer and the next set's target.

effort.text: TICKET-034 — mark a set easy or hard

effortwhy.text:
Per set, not per exercise. No mark = done in good form, as planned.

E (hollow) = easy, push more next time. H (solid) = hard: missed reps, lost form or needed a spot.

Board 5: rate during the rest, the moment the set ends. Optional; tap again to clear.
Board 6: fix a mark later. Unmarked rows carry no extra control; tap a row to open Easy / Hard (and Clear once marked). × still removes the set.
Board 6b: same, with marks in a column beside the set number.
Board 7: next session, set 4's mark rides on the Last time pill.
Board 8: history sheet shows the mark per set; the caption counts them. Date chips stay plain.

No new colours: gold is PR, red is discard. E and H differ in fill (lightness), not hue.

edit.text: TICKET-040 — edit a set before Finish

editwhy.text:
Edit, not remove + re-log: set ids are positions, so edit never moves a set, keeps its mark and starts no rest.

Board 9: Edit joins Easy / Hard / Clear in the strip the row tap already opens.
Board 10: the card switches to EDIT SET 2, prefilled with the logged values. Ghosts and the Last time pill are last session's set 2, not the next set. Cancel / Save set 2. What you had typed for set 5 comes back after.
While editing, the Today list is read-only: no ×, no strip, and a pending Undo waits ("Undo after this edit") rather than being lost. Ids are ordinals, so a remove or undo mid-edit would point the edit at another set.
Board 11: editing during a rest swaps the rest panel for the card; the rest keeps counting. Same refusals as logging, worded "save".
Board 12: Save returns to the rest. Banner, delta and volume re-derive from 67.5; the H mark and position stay.

Swiping to another exercise drops an open edit (the card is per exercise).

editopts.text:
Entry options for TICKET-040.

A (board 9): strip gets Easy / Hard / Clear | Edit. Four controls; reads cluttered.

B (9b): three equal buttons, Easy / Hard / Edit. Clear goes: tapping the chosen mark already clears it (034's toggle), said once in small text. Keeps 034's one-tap marking.

C (9c): no strip. Tapping a row opens the card as EDIT SET 2, with the mark inside it (Felt: Easy / Hard). One place to change anything about a set; mark and numbers save together, Cancel reverts both. Cost: changing only a mark from the list is tap, tap, Save instead of one tap. The rest panel still asks right after each set, so most marks never need the list.

plates.text: TICKET-041 · C1–C2 — plates as a weight unit

plateswhy.text:
Plates = the number on a machine's stack or pin, when the real weight is unknown. Never converted; compares only with plates (same rule as kg vs lb).

C1: plates is a third unit chip next to kg and lb, with one line saying what it means. Set in Manage Workout only: expand a plan exercise, change its unit, Save changes. Collapsed rows show each exercise's fields and unit.
C2: label WEIGHT · PLATES, steppers −1 / +1, Last time pill 5 × 12 (no unit, as today). Rows read "5 plates × 12"; 1 reads "1 plate" (today's code would print "1 plates").
C2 rest: deltas and the best banner in plates: "+1 plate", "6 plates · beat 5 plates from 17 Oct".
C2 after kg: no pill, no ghosts. The notice names the old unit and numbers instead of "a different unit"; rows show no delta, and one caption says why.

Half plates (an add-on weight) can be typed as 4.5; the stepper stays whole.

platesopts.text:
Options for C1–C2.

C1 vs C1b, where the unit is set. CHOSEN: C1 (user, 2026-10-24): the unit is set in Manage Workout only; to change it, change the plan.
C1b (rejected): also on the set card, tap WEIGHT · KG, before set 1 only, saved to the plan. Mixing kg and plates inside one session would break volume and deltas, so it locks after set 1. Costs a new control and a plan write from the logger: more than TICKET-044 stage 1.

C2 vs C2b, volume. CHOSEN: C2 (user, 2026-10-24): "2 sets · 115 plates", shown with its unit. Fair on the same machine.
C2b (rejected): "2 sets", no volume for plates. Loses the volume trend for machine work.

manageopts.text:
Manage Workout around C1. Today's screen has a New switch on both pickers; these replace it.

Add exercise: the dashed button under the list opens the exercise picker (group A designs it). A catalog exercise arrives expanded with its catalog fields. DEFERRED (user, 2026-10-24): no new custom exercises for now, so the Custom board with its starting templates is not built; it stays here for TICKET-045. Any exercise can take one more field from the box at the bottom.

New plan. CHOSEN: first row of the picker's list (user, 2026-10-24). The screen carries no New button; the picker is the only control on top. Tapping New plan turns that row into a name field with Create; the new plan opens with no exercises and saves with its first one.
Rejected: a New button beside the picker. Always visible, one more control on top, and redundant once the list offers it.

No plans yet: an empty picker would be a dead end, so the screen skips it and asks for a name straight away (Create stays disabled until something is typed). After Create it is the same screen as any new plan: the picker shows its name, Exercises reads None yet, Add exercise below. The picker appears from the second plan on, with New plan as its first row.

Wording: "plan", matching the Start screen's "No plans yet · Create a plan" (user, 2026-10-24). The screen title stays Manage Workout.

findwhy.text:
The picker is a full screen opened by Manage Workout's Add exercise, not a dropdown.

A1: search box focused, filters, then Recent: versions you have logged, newest first, with the date. A recent row adds that version directly (no version step). Rows already in the plan read In plan and do nothing (plan save refuses duplicates today).
A2: one row per movement: name, main muscle first then the others, and "19 versions" only when there is more than one.
A3: tapping a movement with versions opens a sheet. The version you used last is preselected and marked "last". Combinations that do not exist (Band × Incline) are disabled, not hidden. One version: no sheet, it is added at once. Equipment typed in the query ("db bench") preselects that version instead.
A3 attachment: a cable movement has an Attachment row (Rope / Straight Bar / V-Bar), shown only for Cable.
A4 typo: no special state. Results come back under "Close matches" when every one is a fuzzy match.
A4 none: says why (every word must match) and suggests fewer words. Nothing to create.

Names with a version use "Movement · Version" here as a stand-in; group B decides the format.

No new custom exercises, for now (user, 2026-10-24): the catalog is the only source. Existing custom exercises in plans and history keep working and are found by name. A missing machine is logged as the closest catalog movement, with a field or (044) a tag. Revisit later: TICKET-045.

Tags (user, 2026-10-24): every tag is treated alike. Grip, stance, pause, bands, chains, belt are chosen in A3 with the version, stored on the plan's exercise and used for every set. Changed later in Manage Workout (board A3 · tags). Not chosen per set. Changing one for a single workout is TICKET-047, with the version switch. C5 only designs how a session with other tags reads in history.

findopts.text:
Options for A.

A1 vs A1b, filters. CHOSEN: A1 (user, 2026-10-24). A1: three menus, Muscle / Equipment / Type, each opens a list. One row, nothing to scroll; muscle is two taps. A1b: muscle groups as chips in view (one tap), equipment and type as menus below. Muscle is the filter people use most; costs a second row.

A2 vs A2b, what a row says about versions. CHOSEN: A2 (user, 2026-10-24). A2: a count, "19 versions". Quiet; you see which in the next step. A2b: the first few by name, "Barbell, Dumbbell, Smith, Machine +4". Tells you before tapping whether your equipment is there; a third line on every row.

A3 vs A3b, incline. CHOSEN: A3 (user, 2026-10-24): incline is an angle of Bench Press. A3: incline is an angle of Bench Press (TICKET-042's recommendation): one row in search, Equipment × Angle in the sheet, and Bench Press then has 19 versions. A3b: Incline Bench Press is its own movement: three rows in search (8, 6, 5 versions), one row of chips in the sheet. People say "incline bench" either way; A3 keeps it under bench, A3b makes the sheet simpler.

names.text: TICKET-041 · B1–B2 — the name with its version

nameopts.text:
CHOSEN: A (2026-10-24; the user leaned B, liked A, and asked for the choice on user-experience grounds).
Why A: it is the convention people already know from logging apps (Hevy names it "Bench Press (Barbell)": movement first, equipment after). The movement leads, and people scanning a list read about the first two words (NN/g), so a plan reads by movement. One string works where only one string fits: the logs filter's selected value, spoken labels, a toast. Middle dot, not brackets, because names already contain brackets: "Pec Deck (Machine Fly)".
Rule that comes with it: never cut a name to one line, wrap to two. Cut, it is the version that disappears. Today the Start plan row and the history sheet title cut to one line; both change.
Plan-level tags join the version part: "Bench Press · Barbell, close grip, pause".

Rejected B (version on its own line): never cut, but every row in every list grows a line, and the logger header gets a third line.
Rejected C (a written name per version, "Incline Dumbbell Bench Press"): versions of one movement do not sort or scan together, and TICKET-046 would have to write ~900 names.

switchwhy.text:
DEFERRED to TICKET-047 (user, 2026-10-24): wanted, not built now. Covers tags too: a different grip or pause for one workout is the same kind of switch.

Decided: a switch is for this workout only, and the plan keeps its version, so next week starts on the planned one again. Changing the plan stays in Manage Workout (same rule as C1). Hevy and Strong do the same by default (their "update the routine?" question at Finish is the part left out).

Before set 1: the exercise is swapped for today. Targets and Last time come from the new version's history.
After sets: logged sets stay on the old version; the new one is added beside it in this workout and starts at set 1.

c35.text: TICKET-041 · C3–C5 — C3, C4 dropped; C5 tags

c35why.text:
DROPPED (user, 2026-10-24), MVP with about 5–10 users: C3 machine settings and C4 per-side reps. Few people would record them, and each adds stored shape and screens. Reps stay plain; a one-arm exercise is still its own version, without a "per side" label. Boards kept for reference.

C5: tags live on the plan (A3), so they change only when the plan changes. These boards are the first session after the plan went from normal to close grip.
History sheet: the selected session's tags join its summary line; the Today column names today's. Date chips stay plain (TICKET-034).

c35opts.text:
Options for C5 (C3 and C3b dropped).

C5 vs C5b, the first session after tags change. CHOSEN: C5 (user, 2026-10-24): smallest change for an MVP; revisit C5b if the explained −10 still misleads.
C5: compare with last time anyway, and say the tags differed: pill "80 × 8 normal grip", a line on the card, a caption under Today. The delta still reads −10 kg, explained but grey.
C5b: take targets from the last session with the same tags (close grip on 3 Oct), so 70 × 8 reads "matched", not −10. If there is none, no targets, as with a unit change. History by version stays one list; only the comparison is filtered.
